question: According to the Hawaii CDL manual, to approximately what psi range should the air compressor build air pressure at governor cut-out?
explanation: The manual states to check that the air compressor builds the air pressure to governor cut-out at approximately 120-140 psi or as specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, In-Cab Inspection - Air Gauge

question: During the hydraulic brake check, after pumping the brake pedal three times, how long must you hold it down while checking that the pedal does not move?
choice_b: 5 seconds
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds, and the pedal should not move (depress) during the five seconds.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: What happens if a CDL applicant fails to perform both components of the hydraulic brake check during the vehicle inspection test?
choice_a: A warning is issued but testing continues
choice_b: The vehicle inspection test results in automatic failure
choice_c: Points are deducted from the Basic Control Skills test
choice_d: The examiner simply repeats the check for the driver
explanation: The manual states that failure to perform both components of the hydraulic brake check will result in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Hydraulic Brake Check

topic: Air Brake Check - Static Leak Test
question: During the one-minute static air brake leak check on a single (non-combination) vehicle, what is the maximum allowable air pressure drop?
choice_b: Two pounds
explanation: The manual states to check that the air pressure does not drop more than three pounds in one minute for a single vehicle, or four pounds for a combination vehicle.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check

topic: Air Brake Check - Static Leak Test
question: For a combination vehicle, what is the maximum allowable air pressure drop during the one-minute static air brake leak check?
choice_b: Four pounds
explanation: The manual specifies the air pressure should not drop more than four pounds in one minute for a combination vehicle during the static leak check.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check

topic: Air Brake Check - Low Air Warning
question: While fanning off air pressure during the air brake check, before what psi level should the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, or flag) activate?
choice_b: Before 65 psi
explanation: The manual states low air warning devices should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi, or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check

question: On a tractor-trailer combination vehicle, within what psi range should the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve close (pop out) as air pressure continues to be fanned off?
explanation: The manual states that at a range between 20-45 psi on a tractor-trailer combination vehicle (or the level specified by the manufacturer), the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve should close (pop out).
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check

question: Failure to correctly perform how many components of the air brake check will result in automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test?
choice_b: Only two
choice_d: Any component, but only if repeated twice
explanation: The manual states that failure to perform all three components of the air brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Air Brake Check

question: During the service brake check, at approximately what speed should you pull forward before applying the service brake and stopping?
choice_b: 10 mph
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service brake, and stop, checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Service Brake Check

question: How does a driver confirm during the inspection test that the parking brake will hold the vehicle?
choice_a: By listening for air leaks near the compressor
choice_b: By gently trying to pull the vehicle forward with the parking brake engaged
choice_d: By checking the tire tread depth
explanation: With air pressure built to governor cutout and the parking brake engaged, the manual says to check that the parking brake will hold the vehicle by gently trying to pull forward with the parking brake on.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Parking Brake Check

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on steering axle tires during a CDL vehicle inspection?
choice_b: 4/32 inch
explanation: The manual requires a minimum tread depth of 4/32 inch on steering axle tires and 2/32 inch on all other tires.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.4 Wheels - Tires

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on tires other than the steering axle tires?
choice_b: 2/32 inch
explanation: The manual specifies a minimum tread depth of 2/32 inch on all tires other than steering axle tires, which require 4/32 inch.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.4 Wheels - Tires

question: How must a driver check tire inflation during the CDL vehicle inspection test?
choice_b: By striking the tires with a mallet
explanation: The manual notes that inflation must be checked using a tire gauge, and that a driver will not get credit for simply kicking the tires or using a mallet.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.4 Wheels - Tires

question: According to the manual, what type of repair is never acceptable on a wheel rim?
choice_b: Welding repairs
explanation: The manual states that rims cannot have welding repairs, and to check for damaged or bent rims and rust trails that may indicate the rim is loose on the wheel.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.4 Wheels - Rims

question: For manual slack adjustors, how far should the brake pushrod move (with the brakes released) when pulled by hand?
choice_b: No more than two inches
choice_d: It should not move at all
explanation: The manual states that for manual slack adjustors, the brake pushrod should not move more than one inch, with the brakes released, when pulled by hand.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.3 Brakes - Slack Adjustors and Pushrods

question: Besides spare electrical fuses (if equipped), what emergency equipment must a driver check for during the in-cab inspection?
choice_b: Three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares, plus a properly charged and mounted fire extinguisher
explanation: The manual directs drivers to check for three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares, and that the fire extinguisher is properly charged and securely mounted.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Emergency Equipment

question: If a commercial motor vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, what must the driver do during the vehicle inspection test?
choice_b: Mention this fact to the examiner
choice_d: Skip the emergency equipment section entirely
explanation: The manual notes that if the vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, the driver must mention this to the examiner.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Emergency Equipment

question: For a vehicle equipped with emissions after-treatment equipment, what must the driver check regarding the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) tank?
choice_a: That the DEF tank is completely empty
choice_b: That the DEF level is more than 1/8th of the tank and the dash DEF indicator works properly
choice_c: That the DEF tank cap has been removed
choice_d: That the DEF tank has been replaced with a new one
explanation: The manual states the driver checks the DEF tank to ensure the level is adequate (more than 1/8th tank) and checks that the DEF indicator on the dash is working properly.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.5 Side of Vehicle - Exhaust System

question: When inspecting the fifth wheel coupling, what must the driver verify about the trailer and skid plate?
choice_a: That the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap
choice_b: That the trailer is raised slightly above the skid plate
choice_c: That the release arm is disengaged
choice_d: That the locking jaws are open
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to check that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate, with no gap, and to check for kingpin lock.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.7 Tractor/Coupling - Kingpin/Apron/Gap

question: If equipped, what position should the fifth wheel release arm be in during the coupling inspection?
choice_a: Disengaged with the safety latch removed
choice_b: The engaged position with the safety latch in place
choice_d: Removed from the vehicle for inspection
explanation: The manual states that, if equipped, the driver must make sure the release arm is in the engaged position and the safety latch is in place.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.2.7 Tractor/Coupling - Release Arm (Fifth Wheel)

question: What must a driver check regarding glad hands when inspecting the front of a trailer?
choice_a: That they are disconnected for storage
choice_b: That they are locked in place and free of damage or air leaks
choice_c: That they are painted a specific color
choice_d: That they are only hand-tight, not fully seated
explanation: The manual states to make sure glad hands are locked in place, free of damage or air leaks, and that the trailer electrical plug is firmly seated and locked in place.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.4.1 Trailer Front - Air/Electrical Connections

question: When inspecting the landing gear on the side of a trailer, what should the driver verify?
choice_a: That it is fully lowered to the ground
choice_b: That it is fully raised, has no missing parts, and the crank handle is secure
choice_c: That it has been removed for the inspection
choice_d: That it is painted amber for visibility
explanation: The manual states to check that the landing gear is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.4.2 Side of Trailer - Landing Gear

question: According to the manual, what do all four versions of the Class A CDL vehicle inspection test include?
choice_a: Only an inspection of the trailer frame
choice_b: An engine start, an in-cab inspection, and an inspection of the coupling system
choice_c: A full road test and a written exam
explanation: The manual states that all four versions of the Class A vehicle inspection test include an engine start, an in-cab inspection, and an inspection of the coupling system.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Class A Vehicle Inspection Test

question: What must happen before a CDL applicant can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: The applicant must pass the Vehicle Inspection test
choice_b: The applicant must complete a full road test
choice_c: The applicant must pass a written exam a second time
choice_d: The applicant must submit a new medical certificate
explanation: The manual states that the Vehicle Inspection must be passed before the applicant can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Vehicle Inspection Test overview (following 11.5.4 Remainder of Coach/Transit Bus)
